summary: The live VGA DAC across every captured save state in tools/dosbox/save/ matches BIOS-default EGA exactly (distance 0). WIZ6_MAIN (catalog entry from the INT 10h AX=1002h site at wroot 0x209B) and WIZ6_DUNGEON (wroot 0x2105) are nonzero distance from every observed DAC (4845 and 5015 respectively, identical across all saves) — i.e. neither has ever been programmed in any state we've captured. This directly contradicts a claim in docs/re/findings/wfont-highlight-render.json that 'palette[5] in WIZ6_MAIN = (170,255,0) yellow-green' is what the user sees on the highlighted menu row; under the actual runtime DAC, palette[5] = EGA_DEFAULT[5] = (170,0,170) MAGENTA. The current render path's choice to use EGA_DEFAULT as the lookup table for index→RGB is therefore CORRECT — it matches the hardware. The error is in the prior finding's color narrative, not in our rendering.
key_insight: The two engine palette-load sites (wroot 0x209B, 0x2105) exist in code but are not actually reached in any gameplay state we've captured. Either they're guarded by an unmet condition (video-mode flag, hardware capability detection) or they're reached only during transitions we haven't snapshotted. Either way: render against EGA_DEFAULT and the colors will match the engine's framebuffer.
method: Used mcp__wiz6__dosbox_identify_palette across save states 1, 2, 5, 10 (covering game_state=0xffff and game_state=1). All four reported exact match to ega-default (distance 0), wiz6-main at 4845, wiz6-dungeon at 5015. The decoded live DAC RGB triples are byte-identical to the EGA_DEFAULT table in @wiz6/data.

findings.claim: Live VGA DAC across all captured saves = BIOS-default EGA palette, distance 0.
WIZ6_MAIN (the catalog entry from wroot 0x209B's AX=1002h load) is never the active DAC in any captured save.

evidence.note: Distance is identical across all four saves, suggesting WIZ6_MAIN is loaded ZERO times during the captured paths — not loaded then overwritten, but never programmed at all. (If it were overwritten back to default, distances could plausibly vary.)

findings.claim: The 'menu-selected' highlight cell with original attr=5, written by df85 as cell.attr_byte=0x50, renders as black-on-MAGENTA (170, 0, 170), not black-on-yellow-green. The prior finding's '(170, 255, 0) yellow' is a WIZ6_MAIN palette claim and WIZ6_MAIN is not the live DAC.

evidence.user_visual_expectation: UNVERIFIED — the prior chain of reasoning assumed yellow; user's actual reference image of the original game has not been pixel-sampled at the highlighted cell

implications: USER OBSERVATION: the original game renders selected menu rows as yellow-on-black (or black-on-yellow). Under live DAC = EGA_DEFAULT, that's palette[14] = (255, 255, 85). NOT palette[5] = (170, 0, 170) magenta.

wfont-highlight-render.json's claim that the menu highlight resolves to 'palette index 5 = yellow-green via WIZ6_MAIN' is wrong on TWO counts: (1) the function it identifies as df85 at wroot 0x22B7 isn't what wbase actually calls — the wbase E8-call-target math at 0x23DC and 0x27BD lands on thunk 0xDF85, which per the thunk-delta law resolves to wroot ~0x24E9 (off by ~0x232 bytes); (2) the live DAC is EGA_DEFAULT, not WIZ6_MAIN, so a palette[5] background would be magenta, not yellow-green.

The 1bpp wfont0 sheet is reused across multiple engine render primitives. The user reports seeing it used for both 'black-on-color' highlights and 'color-on-black' text in different UI contexts. The prior subagent traced ONE such call path and assumed it was the menu-cursor path; that mapping is unverified.

Pragmatic state: the current viewer's '{1:0, 8:14}' override on the 4bpp wfont3 panel-variant glyph produces yellow-on-black that visually matches the engine. It is NOT engine-call-path-faithful, but the OUTPUT pixel-grid is approximately correct under EGA_DEFAULT.

Per-scene-palette switching (TODO #002) should treat EGA_DEFAULT as the actual baseline. WIZ6_MAIN and WIZ6_DUNGEON catalog entries should be retained as RE artifacts but flagged 'not observed as active DAC in any captured save'.

open_questions.claim: When (which call path) does INT 10h AX=1002h at wroot 0x209B actually run, given we never see WIZ6_MAIN in a save? Possibly gated on a hardware-detect flag (e.g. only on real EGA, not VGA) or only reached during a state we haven't captured (e.g. mid-cutscene, total party kill graveyard transition).
What color does the actual game reference image show at the highlighted menu row? Need a pixel sample of an authoritative screenshot.
